newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil lower on softer crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil lower on softer crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices slipped on Tuesday on softer crude prices, with the physical market taking the lead from the swaps market, traders said.
Lower prices were also attributable to softer IPE gas oil futures with March last traded at $177 a tonne, down 50 cents.
Traders said the market was nervously monitoring talk that a U.S. trading house would be bringing in a VLCC of gas oil from Western Europe to this region in late March.
They said this VLCC could be part of the 585,000 tonnes of gas oil physical deliveries against the February IPE futures.

But some traders noted that the arbitrage to East Asia might not be attactive enough to bring such a large cargo, especially with China not yet fully committed to buying, while Indonesia has not indicated its requirements for March.
Traders said part of the cargo might head for the U.S. Gulf Coast instead.
They also noted that another U.S. trader who was said to have planned to bring in a VLCC of gas oil following the IPE expiry late last year, finally did not bring in that cargo to this region.
Some traders said China would not be in a hurry to buy March gas oil.

China's low enquiry level of $198 a tonne, c-and-f, indicated that Chinese buyers did not want to rush its purchases as they were very aware that this would only force up prices beyond their ability to pay, they said.
Sri Lanka has no immediate plans to buy more gas oil for power generation to compensate for possible shortage of hydropower during the current dry season, a Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) source said.

He noted that the Ceylon Electricity Board has decided to raise thermal generation to avoid power cuts and for the time being there has been no orders from the board to import extra gas oil for generation.

He said if an emergency occurs, such as if the drought persisted until April, the board could place their import orders within two weeks. Sri Lanka has bought about 200,000 tonnes of gas oil, jet fuel and gasoline during January-March to make up for shortages during the shutdown of its 60,000-barrel- -per-day Sapugaskande refinery since January 15. The refinery is due to restart sometime next week.

Physical gas oil was offered lower with a 150,000 barrel parcel for March 16-20 seen at $25.70, compared with Monday's $26.00. A bid for 200,000 barrels lifting March 5-9 was seen at $25.20, compared with Monday's $25.70.
Gas oil swaps was also weaker with March trading at $25.95 a barrel, down from Monday's trade of $26.25.
Jet fuel swaps continued to firm with the jet/gas oil regrade seen at $2.65/$2.85 a barrel, up from Monday's $2.40/$2.70.
